title: Your First Angular App 🖥️
description: Run the development server, make your first change, and see live reload magic.

slides.title: Start the Dev Server 🏃
slides.content: Open a terminal inside your project folder (`my-first-app`) and run:

slides.title: What Happens? 👀
slides.content:
1. The CLI compiles your TypeScript & templates.
2. It bundles everything and starts a local web server.
3. Open your browser to **http://localhost:4200**.

You’ll see a page with the Angular logo and some text. That’s your app!

quizData.question: `ng serve` builds the app and opens it automatically in a new browser window.
quizData.explanation: `ng serve` starts the dev server but does not automatically open the browser. You must navigate to `http://localhost:4200` manually (or use `ng serve --open`).

slides.title: The App Component File
slides.content: Open `src/app/app.component.ts`. You’ll see something like this:

slides.title: Key Parts Explained 🔑
slides.content:
* `@Component` is a **decorator** – it tells Angular this class is a component.
* `selector: 'app-root'` – the custom HTML tag used in `index.html`.
* `templateUrl` – points to the HTML file that defines the view.
* `title` is a class property we can display in the template.

slides.title: Edit the Template ✏️
slides.codeSnippet:
Hello, Progly!

Welcome to my first Angular app.

{{ title }}

slides.title: Live Reload 🔄
slides.content:
Save the file – the browser updates automatically! That’s **live reload** in action.

The `{{ title }}` syntax is called **interpolation**. It pulls the value from the component’s class into the HTML.

quizData.question: In Angular templates, we use {{ }} to display component ______.
quizData.explanation: Double curly braces `{{ }}` evaluate a component property and insert its value into the DOM.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## `ng serve --open`

Add the `--open` (or `-o`) flag to automatically open the browser:

```bash
ng serve -o
```
